author: Rida Morwa
title: We are currently in a "raging bull market," and during the y
text:
We are currently in a "raging bull market," and during the year 2017 "growth stocks" have strongly outperformed "value stocks," and notably "value dividend stocks." Most investors have been chasing the same stocks, pushing their prices higher and higher.
As recently documented by Bespoke, the 50 highest yielding stocks in the S&P 500 at the start of 2017 are up in price by just 5.35% as of mid-November 2017 , while the 81 non-dividend paying stocks in the S&P 500 are up 18.97% . This picture did not change much through December 31, 2017.
Why did High-Yield Sectors underperform in 2017? The weakness in several "High-Yield" Sectors during 2017 can be attributed to two main reasons:
Investors piling up on "Momentum Stocks" : Many of the high dividend sectors are lower growth sectors, such as Property REITs, Midstream MLPs and Business Development Companies (or BDCs), and were out of favor in 2017. Investors have been under-allocating to these sectors in favor of growth and momentum stocks such as Technology and FANG stocks (FANG being Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ) and Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL )). The market has been clearly favoring momentum stocks with high P/E multiples and reasonably strong growth trajectories. Some growth stocks are even trading at crazy valuations. For example, Amazon ( AMZN ) trades at a Price/Earnings ratio (or P/E ratio) of over 400 times earnings, while Facebook trades at a P/E ratio of 40 times earnings. Tax Reforms ambiguities : Another factor that can be attributed to weakness in several high-dividend sectors is the Tax Reform proposals. Before the tax reforms were finalized, there was a great deal of uncertainty surrounding pass-through entities (such as MLPs, Property REITs and BDCs), with many investors speculating that the reforms will be unfavorable to these sectors.
